title: Finite type lifts along a nilpotent ideal (ring version)
statement: Let $A'\to B'$ be a ring map of commutative rings and $I\subseteq A'$ a nilpotent ideal ($I^{n+1}=0$ for some $n\ge0$). If the induced ring map $A'/I\to B'/IB'$ is of finite type (i.e. $B'/IB'$ is a finitely generated $A'/I$-algebra), then $A'\to B'$ is of finite type. (Proof: choose $b_1,\dots,b_m\in B'$ whose images generate $B'/IB'$ over $A'/I$, let $R=A'[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'$, $x_j\mapsto b_j$; then $R/IR=(A'/I)[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'/IB'$ is surjective, i.e. $B'=N+IB'$ for the image $N$ of $R$, as $A'$-modules; by Nakayama's lemma for the nilpotent ideal $I$ (Algebra 00DV (11), which follows from part (9): $M=IM$ with $I$ nilpotent implies $M=0$, applied to $M=B'/N$) $R\to B'$ is surjective.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW (label lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian), proof, 'The translation of (2) into algebra' (stated there with I^2=0; the argument uses only Algebra, Lemma 00DV (label lemma-NAK) part (11), which holds for any nilpotent I)

proof.text: (Generators and the polynomial ring.) Write $\pi:B'\to\bar B:=B'/IB'$ for the quotient map. Since $A'/I\to\bar B$ is of finite type, by definition (Algebra, Definition 00F3) there are $m\in\mathbf N$ and a surjection of $A'/I$-algebras $(A'/I)[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to\bar B$; let $\beta_j\in\bar B$ be the image of $y_j$, so $\bar B$ is generated as an $A'/I$-algebra by $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m$. As $\pi$ is surjective, choose $b_j\in B'$ with $\pi(b_j)=\beta_j$. Let $R=A'[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ and let $\varphi:R\to B'$ be the $A'$-algebra map with $x_j\mapsto b_j$; put $N:=\varphi(R)=A'[b_1,\dots,b_m]\subseteq B'$, an $A'$-subalgebra, in particular an $A'$-submodule of $B'$. Regard $\varphi$ as a homomorphism of $A'$-modules.

source.place: Algebra, Definition 00F3 (label definition-finite-type); More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW, proof, 'The translation of (2) into algebra' (the map A'[x_1,...,x_n] -> B' with A[x_1,...,x_n] -> B surjective)

proof.text: ($R/IR\to B'/IB'$ is surjective, i.e. $B'=N+IB'$.) The composite $\pi\circ\varphi:R\to\bar B$ is the $A'$-algebra map with $x_j\mapsto\beta_j$; its image is the $A'$-subalgebra of $\bar B$ generated by $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m$. Since $A'$ acts on $\bar B$ through $A'\to A'/I$, this is the $A'/I$-subalgebra generated by the $\beta_j$, which is $\bar B$ by step 1. So $\pi\circ\varphi$ is surjective: for every $b\in B'$ there is $P\in R$ with $b-\varphi(P)\in\ker\pi=IB'$. Hence $B'=N+IB'$ as $A'$-modules; equivalently, since $\varphi(IR)\subseteq IB'$, the induced $A'$-linear map $R/IR\to B'/IB'$ is surjective.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW (label lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian), proof, 'The translation of (2) into algebra: ... Nakayama's lemma applied to a map A'[x_1,...,x_n] -> B' such that A[x_1,...,x_n] -> B is surjective'

proof.text: (Nakayama.) Apply Nakayama's lemma for a nilpotent ideal [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] (Algebra 00DV (11)) to the ring $A'$, its nilpotent ideal $I$ ($I^{n+1}=0$) and the $A'$-module homomorphism $\varphi:R\to B'$: by step 2 the induced map $R/IR\to B'/IB'$ is surjective, hence $\varphi$ is surjective, i.e. $N=B'$. (No finiteness of $B'$ as an $A'$-module is needed, since $I$ is nilpotent rather than merely contained in the Jacobson radical.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DV (label lemma-NAK), part (11); as used in More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW, proof, 'The translation of (2) into algebra'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By step 3, $\varphi:A'[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'$ is a surjection of $A'$-algebras, so $A'\to B'$ is of finite type by Algebra, Definition 00F3 ($B'$ is generated as an $A'$-algebra by $b_1,\dots,b_m$). (In Mathlib this is Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial'', Mathlib/RingTheory/FiniteType.lean:174.)

split_report.summary: Proof written from More on Morphisms 09ZW, 'The translation of (2) into algebra', in four steps: (1) generators of B'/IB' (Definition 00F3) lifted to B' and the A'-algebra map phi: A'[x_1..x_m] -> B' (elementary); (2) R/IR -> B'/IB' surjective, i.e. B' = N + IB' as A'-modules (elementary); (3) Nakayama for the nilpotent ideal I of A', Algebra 00DV (11), applied to phi as an A'-linear map: new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent (absent from Mathlib: Mathlib's Nakayama lemmas all need finite generation and the Jacobson radical; surjective_of_mkQ_comp_surjective needs IsPrecomplete/IsHausdorff instances that Mathlib does not provide for nilpotent ideals); (4) conclusion by Definition 00F3 (Mathlib Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''). Working over A' instead of over R with the ideal IR (as the statement's sketch did) avoids proving IR nilpotent. The statement's parenthetical misnumbered the part of 00DV: 'M = IM, I nilpotent => M = 0' is part (9); the part applied is (11); the sketch was corrected accordingly, the statement proper is unchanged. No Nakayama node existed in the DAG (lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators is the local-ring version). Whole statement not in Mathlib (searches recorded); nothing in the source repository (grep of WeilConjectures for finiteType/FiniteType with nilpotent: no hits).
